_about: Learning paths: short, ordered routes through the library, each with a finish line. `topic` is the small label above the title. A step is the folder of a track (all its written modules, in order) or of a single module. Order matters: it is the order a reader follows. `next` is the path to suggest once this one is finished. Run `npm run check:paths` after editing.

paths.title: Production Core
paths.goal: Master the core of production backend services: HTTP protocols, API routing and validation, authentication, transactional SQL, and multi-tier caching.
paths.audience: Engineers building backend services that must handle real-world traffic reliably, securely, and correctly.
prerequisites: Basic programming in any backend language (Go, Java, Python, TypeScript, C#)
Basic SQL and relational database knowledge

milestone.title: Idempotent Payment & Order Engine
milestone.description: Design and implement a concurrent payment processing API with distributed locks, idempotency keys, and zero double-charge race conditions.
deliverables: Distributed lock with automated TTL and singleflight protection
Concurrency stress test simulating 1,000 parallel checkout requests

paths.title: High-Scale & Distributed Systems
paths.goal: Design and scale distributed backends: Kafka streaming, gRPC microservices, consensus, sharding, sagas, and system design patterns.
paths.audience: Backend developers and engineers preparing for senior roles and system design interviews.
prerequisites: Production Core, or comfortable with databases, caching, and APIs

milestone.title: Distributed Sliding-Window Rate Limiter
milestone.description: Build a high-throughput multi-tier rate limiting service using Redis sliding logs/token buckets with Kafka dead-letter queues under failover.
deliverables: Sliding-window counter implementation with Redis Lua scripts
Chaos test simulating Redis node failure with graceful fallback

paths.title: Observability & DevOps
paths.goal: Package, orchestrate, monitor, and deploy backend microservices: Docker containers, Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD GitOps, Prometheus metrics, and SRE incident response.
paths.audience: Backend engineers who need full operational ownership of their services in production.
prerequisites: A runnable backend service to containerize

milestone.title: Self-Healing Canary Deployment
milestone.description: Set up a complete automated CI/CD and canary deployment pipeline that monitors p99 latency and error budgets, auto-rolling back upon degradation.
deliverables: Prometheus alerts for p99 latency and 5xx error rate
Automated canary rollback script on simulated traffic errors

paths.title: AI Backend Engineering
paths.goal: Engineer robust AI-native backends: token economics, model serving, OpenAI/Gemini APIs, vector embeddings, and semantic caching.
paths.audience: Backend developers integrating large language models and vector search into production software.
prerequisites: Can call HTTP APIs from backend code
Basic vector and linear algebra intuition

milestone.title: Production RAG & Semantic Cache Gateway
milestone.description: Build an API gateway that intercepts LLM queries, performs vector cosine similarity search in a semantic cache, and falls back to streaming model responses.
deliverables: Semantic cache query engine in Redis/PgVector with <15ms response
Token streaming handler with graceful provider fallback

paths.title: Backend foundations
paths.goal: Follow a request from the browser to the database and back, and learn to build APIs that are correct and secure.
paths.audience: New to backend work, or self-taught with gaps to fill.

paths.title: Fast, observable and reliable
paths.goal: Take a working service and make it hold up: caching, background jobs and realtime, monitoring, and the patterns distributed systems rely on.
paths.audience: You can build an API and now need it to survive real traffic.
prerequisites: You can build and deploy a basic API

paths.title: System design interview sprint
paths.goal: Learn the building blocks interviews lean on, then practise the structure of a system design answer.
prerequisites: Comfortable with databases, caching and queues at a basic level

paths.title: Linux and Git, the working basics
paths.goal: Get comfortable in a Linux shell and keep your work safe and reviewable in Git.
paths.audience: Developers who still avoid the terminal.

paths.title: Docker and Kubernetes
paths.goal: Package a service in a container, then run and scale it on Kubernetes.
paths.audience: You can build an app and now need to ship it.
prerequisites: You have an app to package

paths.title: How language models work
paths.goal: Understand what a token is, how a language model predicts text, and how the transformer architecture works.
paths.audience: Developers who use LLMs and want to know what is inside.

paths.title: Build with the OpenAI API
paths.goal: Call a hosted model from your own code, then compare the providers and route between them.
paths.audience: You can code and want to add an LLM to a product.
prerequisites: You can call an HTTP API from code

paths.title: Low-level design
paths.goal: Learn object-oriented design, SOLID and the classic design patterns, then practise the standard interview problems.
paths.audience: Preparing for LLD rounds, or tired of tangled code.
